# SMT Solving

## SAT Solving

1. Equivalent CNF formula contains $2^n$ clauses (each time we must distribuate: $A \lor (B \land C) = (A \lor B) \land (A \lor C))$

3. Example
$$P = r \land (q \lor \neg r) \land (s \lor \neg r) \land (p \lor \neg q \lor \neg s) \land (\neg p \lor \neg q \lor \neg s)$$
$$P[r] = q \land s \land (p \lor \neg q \lor \neg s) \land (\neg p \lor \neg q \lor \neg s)$$
$$P[r, q] = s \land (p \lor \neg s) \land (\neg p \lor \neg s)$$
$$P[r, q, s] = p \land \neg p$$
$$P[r, q, s, p] = False$$

4. Candy box

$$P = ((A \lor B \lor C) \land (A \Longrightarrow B) \land (\neg A \Longrightarrow \neg B) \land ((A \land B) \Longrightarrow C) \land ((\neg A \land \neg B) \Longrightarrow \neg C)) \Longrightarrow (A \land B \land C)$$
$$P = ((A \lor B \lor C) \land (\neg A \lor B) \land (A \lor \neg B) \land (\neg A \lor \neg B \lor C) \land (A \lor B \lor \neg C)) \Longrightarrow (A \land B \land C)$$

$A \Longrightarrow B$

To check if proof $P$ is valid:

proof that $\neg P$ is unsatifiable !!

So $\neg (A \Longrightarrow B) \equiv A \land \neg B$ is unsatifiable

$$\neg P = (A \lor B \lor C) \land (\neg A \lor B) \land (A \lor \neg B) \land (\neg A \lor \neg B \lor C) \land (A \lor B \lor \neg C) \land (\neg A \lor \neg B \lor \neg C)$$
$$\neg P[A] = B \land (\neg B \lor C) \land (\neg B \lor \neg C)$$
$$\neg P[A, B] = C \land \neg C$$
$$\neg P[A, B, C] = False$$

So $\neg P$ is unsatifiable so $P$ is valid !

5. Proof by refutation

E contains NO positive OR NO negative clauses

E contains NO positive clause

$$(\neg a_1 \lor b \lor \cdots) \land (\neg a_2 \lor c \lor \cdots) \land \cdots$$

Set to false every literal appearing negeted in every clause
 => contradiction, E is satisfied !!!

E contains NO negative clauses

$$(a_1 \lor \neg b \lor \cdots) \land (a_2 \lor \neg c \lor \cdots) \land \cdots$$
 
 set to true every literal appearing without negation in every clause
 => E is satisfied, contradiction
